citation: Dittus, F.W. & Boelter, L.M.K. (1930). 'Heat transfer in automobile radiators of tubular type.' Univ. California Publ. Engr. 2(13):443-461.
notes: Famous provenance caveat: what handbooks call 'Dittus-Boelter' differs in coefficient and exponent from the original paper. Bounds (Re > 10000, 0.7 <= Pr <= 160) cited via Bergman/Incropera 2011 sec. 8.5 restatement; primary paper not directly verified.

citation: Forrest, E. C., Hu, L.-W., Buongiorno, J., & McKrell, T. J. (2014). 'Convective Heat Transfer in a High Aspect Ratio Mini-Channel Heated on One Side.' Journal of Heat Transfer 138(2):021704.
notes: Tests 5 closures simultaneously (Modified Sparrow-Cur, Dittus-Boelter, Gnielinski, Petukhov, Sieder-Tate) on a one-sided heated narrow rectangular mini-channel at Re 10000-70000, Pr 2.2-5.4 (water 30-80 degC). Table 4 reports per-closure MAE; Figure 5 shows per-point data including the sub-critical (Re ~3800-3950) region used for visual-estimate digitization. SAND2014-18834J / OSTI 1295764.

citation: Gnielinski, V. (1976). 'New equations for heat and mass transfer in turbulent pipe and channel flow.' Int. Chem. Engr. 16:359-368.
notes: Modified Petukhov correlation; transition + fully turbulent pipe/channel flow. Stated validity: Re 3000-5e6, Pr 0.5-2000. Extends Petukhov's lower-Re bound (10000 → 3000) via explicit transition coverage. Primary text directly verified per the calibration corpus's gnielinski-1976 confirmed bounds.

citation: Jin, Y., Zhao, P., Wan, T., Chen, Z., Liu, K., Wang, X., Li, Y. & Wan, Y. (2023). 'Experimental investigation of buoyancy effects on the heat transfer of supercritical carbon dioxide in a vertical tube.' Annals of Nuclear Energy 188: 109825.
notes: USTC / Institute of Plasma Physics CAS. Local wall temperature, HTC, and Nu measured along a vertical heated tube (inner diameter 7.74 mm) for supercritical CO2, both upward and downward flow, over P 7.8-10 MPa, mass flux 138.3-512.1 kg/m2 s, heat flux 29-60.3 kW/m2, inlet temperature 14-33 C (T_pc ~33.5 C at 7.8 MPa). Nu uncertainty ~9.3%. Heat-transfer deterioration (HTD) occurs only in upward flow. Five existing correlations (Dittus-Boelter, Gupta, Jackson, Zhu, Kim) are tested against the data and found to diverge, especially in HTD; a new correlation with a buoyancy parameter (Bu) is proposed. Properties from NIST REFPROP.

citation: Petukhov, B.S. (1970). 'Heat Transfer and Friction in Turbulent Pipe Flow with Variable Physical Properties.' Advances in Heat Transfer 6:503-564.
notes: High-accuracy turbulent-pipe correlation using friction factor as a free parameter. Stated validity: Re 10000-5e6, Pr 0.5-2000. Superseded for transition (Re 2300-10000) coverage by Gnielinski 1976. Primary paper not directly verified; bounds cited via Bergman/Incropera 2011 sec. 8.5 restatement chain.

citation: Sieder, E.N. & Tate, G.E. (1936). 'Heat transfer and pressure drop of liquids in tubes.' Ind. Eng. Chem. 28(12):1429-1435.
notes: Adds the (mu/mu_w)^0.14 viscosity-ratio correction for large wall-bulk temperature differences. Bounds cited via Bergman/Incropera 2011 sec. 8.5 restatement; primary paper not directly verified.

citation: Sparrow, E. M. & Cur, N. (1982). 'Turbulent Heat Transfer in a Symmetrically or Asymmetrically Heated Flat Rectangular Duct With Flow Separation at Inlet.' Journal of Heat Transfer 104:82-89.
notes: Original form: Nu = 0.0464 Re^0.76 at fixed Pr=2.5, isothermal wall, alpha*=0.0556, Re 10000-45000. Mass-transfer experiment converted to heat transfer via Chilton-Colburn analogy. Modified by Forrest 2014 to extend Pr range via explicit Pr^(1/3) factor and adjust coefficient. Primary paper not directly verified; cited via Forrest 2014 restatement.

citation: Tam, L.M. & Ghajar, A.J. (1998). 'The unusual behavior of local heat transfer coefficient in a circular tube with a bell-mouth inlet.' Experimental Thermal and Fluid Science 16(3): 187-194.
notes: Oklahoma State University. Local peripheral Nusselt number measured along a horizontal electrically-heated circular tube (inside diameter 1.584 cm, L/D=385), uniform wall heat flux, ethylene-glycol/water mixtures, across laminar/transition/turbulent regimes, for reentrant, square-edged, and bell-mouth inlets plus three inlet-screen disturbance levels. Local bulk ranges: Re ~280-49000, Pr ~4-158, Gr ~1000-2.5e5, Nu ~13-258. HTC uncertainty ~9%. Reports two anomalies vs standard assumptions: (1) for a bell-mouth inlet the laminar boundary layer persists far downstream, producing a transition-region Nu dip that extends to x/D=100-175 (vs <25 for the turbulent entrance); (2) the measured fully-developed laminar Nu is far above the analytical 4.364 owing to buoyancy-driven secondary flow.
